documents.title: Finite-Time Singularity Formation for the Three-Dimensional Euler Equations

families.name: The finite expansion and the mean

topics.name: The singular Euler solution
topics.description: The smooth odd periodic initial data, maximal Euler solution and conclusions of Theorem 1.1.

topics.name: Exact waves and the preceding frame
topics.description: The Craik–Criminale wave, its pressure, scaled coordinates and the frame of the preceding wave.

topics.name: The wave and its amplification
topics.description: The strong shear limit, additive comparison, reference solution, positive couplings and successor crossing.

topics.name: The endpoint problem and its Hölder inverse
topics.description: The displacement with two end conditions, coercivity and the mean inverse developed in Section 4 and Appendix A.

topics.name: The initial wave and the common sequence
topics.description: The stationary first wave, parameter schedule, next-wave choice and the common inductive sequence.

topics.name: Localized waves and profiles
topics.description: The transported phase, localized amplitude, narrow periodic profile and curl completion.

topics.name: The finite expansion
topics.description: The transverse equation, leading oscillation, mean terms and successive finite hierarchy profiles.

topics.name: The truncated parent and its coefficients
topics.description: Frequency truncation of the parent flow, its coefficient fields and the central wave data.

topics.name: Finite-order estimates for the mean
topics.description: The phase-independent correction, the integrated inverse and the finite-order bounds of Section 5.

topics.name: The approximate Euler solution
topics.description: Evaluation of profiles in physical space, the cutoff derivative and the approximate Euler residual.

topics.name: Pressure, central gradient and flow
topics.description: Pressure readout, the central rank-one contribution and control of the new flow.

topics.name: The limit and its terminal behavior
topics.description: Closed-slab velocity convergence, preterminal smoothness, central vorticity growth and the maximal time.

topics.name: Frequency cutoff and finite norms
topics.description: The Fourier cutoff, parameter inequalities and finite coefficient estimates in Appendices B–D.

topics.name: Smooth terminal regularity away from the origin
topics.description: The specialized auxiliary construction, mixed derivative estimates and the smooth extension through the terminal time.
